title: Stop interrupted TYPE and DIR before consuming invalid syscall results
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:5392 invokes INT 23h and returns before servicing the interrupted call; int21.c:5337 only sets the resident recovery latch. os/milton/command.c:2797 treats the unchanged AH=3Fh request register as a read count, and :2809 writes that count from a 128-byte stack buffer without testing the latch or bounding got. Thus an interrupted read can turn EAX=0x3F00 into 16128 output bytes. command.c:2741 ignores the same latch after the DIR /P key wait and :2766 continues enumeration. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed p.159 / PDF244 (evidence/manual-page-244.txt); ADR-0003 DEC-16 Fork A; PRD 6.1. Cancellation must not manufacture file bytes. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend harness/diff/fat_diff/test_dos_break.c and the INT21 host seam with Ctrl-C at read, write and DIR pause boundaries. Verify CLOSE and all stdin/stdout restoration paths. Replay controlshort and gaps2 on copied disks under QEMU, require an immediate usable prompt, no later HUGE/F299 lines and zero non-file bytes; also redirect TYPE and compare the committed prefix independently. Add a mutant that omits the interrupted check or permits got > sizeof(chunk); it must fail the byte-boundary and cancellation checks. Scope: Keep child-program INT 23h termination intact. This is a returning resident-call completion bug, not another request to add BREAK ON checkpoints (initech-bsy.4). Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-controlshort-ctrlc.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-gaps2-dir-break.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-control-verification.json; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-controlshort-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-gaps2-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/HUGE.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume_driver.py.

title: Transfer batch control on a plain invocation and reserve return for CALL
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3595 sends every resolved BAT to run_batch_invoke; :4695 always nests run_batch and :4636 restores the previous frame. The plain invocation has no transfer-control result distinguishing it from BL_CALL at :4581. The shared g_batch_buf also needs explicit ownership when frames transfer or return. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed p.142 / PDF227 (evidence/manual-page-227.txt); shipped Reference ch4-batch.tex CALL entry. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add an execution-level C host oracle for parent -> child -> grandchild with both plain invocation and CALL, including IF/FOR bodies. Replay resume_driver.py batch on QEMU: CHILD=arg appears, SHOULD-NOT-RETURN does not, while CALL runs its post-call sentinel. Mutant: route a plain invocation through CALL-style frame restoration; require the forbidden sentinel to make the oracle red. Scope: Keep this pickup on frame transfer and buffer ownership; the batch termination question is B14. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-batch-flow.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-batch-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/CHAIN.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/CHILD.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-227.txt.

title: Execute complete batch files or reject an oversized script before execution
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4212 caps the shared batch buffer at 4096 bytes; batch_load_file at :4375 silently stops at the cap and returns a normal length at :4396. run_batch at :4614 interprets the prefix as a complete file, so the final commands disappear without an error. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:19-25 promises sequential execution; CLAUDE.md Rule 2 forbids silently incomplete success. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend a C execution/PAL oracle at lengths 4095/4096/4097 and the BIG.BAT length, with split lines, labels and CALL reloads crossing the boundary. QEMU B063 must execute BIG-END then BIG-RETURNED, or reject the whole oversized file visibly before BIG-BEGIN. Mutant: restore silent 4096-byte truncation; the final sentinel or reject-before-side-effects assertion must fail. Scope: A streaming/re-reading interpreter is preferable for full compatibility; an explicit all-or-nothing size refusal is the bounded safety fix. Merely raising the constant leaves the defect at the next boundary. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite4-B063-batch-long.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite4-B063.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/BIG.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/B063.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite.py.

title: Resolve qualified executable suffixes and preserve meaningful EXEC failures
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:1319 makes an explicit path a single candidate and :1336 appends only .COM, omitting .EXE/.BAT. run_external at :3612 discards every nonzero EXEC error and :3616 reports Bad command. For the audited GUI files, loader.c:367 rejects e_minalloc beyond the DOS arena but returns LOADER_ERR_BAD_FORMAT; kmain.c:813 maps that to DOS 0Bh, not a memory-specific result. Header arithmetic independently confirms 123 needs 298240 bytes versus 65168 available, WORD 491472 versus 79792. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:32; ADR-0003 DEC-08a.2/.3 and DEC-11; spec/memory_map.h:276/:382/:389; ADR-0013 AC-3 DEC-AC3-1 defines FLAIR GUI launch separately from DOS EXEC. evidence/recovery-extra-verification.json preserves the original MZ headers. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend os/milton/test_command.c candidate planning with qualified COM/EXE/BAT suffix search and explicit-extension controls. Extend test_mzload.c with the audited header geometry to distinguish insufficient memory from invalid format. QEMU followup must run qualified BATCH2 without .BAT; native 123/WORD may still be refused but must receive the actual memory/launch-context diagnosis. Keep test-flair-app-launch green. Mutants: qualified paths try only COM, or map every existing-file EXEC refusal to Bad command; each must be detected. Scope: Do not expand DOS memory limits, shrink BSS reserves or force FLAIR tenants through the DOS ABI to satisfy L040. It is a diagnostic defect; direct DOS execution of these GUI tenants is not an established contract. No TSR is used, so initech-h4bk is not this failure. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-commands-env.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/BATCH2.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-app123-qualified.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-appword-qualified.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-app123-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-appword-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/recovery-extra-verification.json.

title: Expose the child exit status after COMMAND /C
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4713 saves g_errorlevel before the secondary command; run_external at :3609 correctly latches the child result, then builtin_command at :4727 unconditionally restores the old errorlevel and loses it. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:185-186 and MS-DOS 3.3 IF, Reference printed p.147, define ERRORLEVEL from the last program. Capture real DOS 3.3 COMMAND /C exit propagation before locking exact secondary-shell edge cases. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the secondary-command execution oracle with ERR0.COM/ERR7.COM directly, through /C, through nested /C and with prior nonzero parent status; retain private environment and EXIT isolation. Replay advanced-misc under QEMU and require CHILD-EXIT7 and DIRECT-EXIT7, not CHILD-STATUS-LOST. Mutant: restore the saved parent status after /C; the child-status assertion must fail. Scope: Keep status ownership explicit for a builtin or failed lookup that does not run a program; do not overwrite unrelated parent state. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/advanced-misc-errorlevel-shift.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/advanced-misc-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/more-fixtures/ERR7.COM; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/more-fixtures/ERR0.COM; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prepare_more.py.

title: Complete FIND file operands, quoted strings, validation and result status
description: Root cause: os/milton/find_program.asm:62 scans past ordinary operand characters and :134 always reads handle 0; file-operand opening was never implemented. At :109 every quote closes a string and :123 overwrites nlen for subsequent quote groups, so doubled quotes can produce an empty final needle. Unknown option letters fall through at :93. The normal exit at :254 always returns 0, even when count is zero; parameter errors return 1 at :263. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed pp.72-73 / PDF157-158 (evidence/manual-page-157.txt and manual-page-158.txt), for named files, quoted literal strings and switches. L017's exact malformed-argument status of 2 is auditor memory, not established by those pages; mint actual DOS 3.3 match/no-match/parse-error statuses before changing that branch. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test-find-filter with one/multiple named files, stdin as a control, doubled quotes, /V /C /N, valid documented Initech /I, invalid switches and batch ERRORLEVEL tests. Compare bytes, headings and exit statuses to a real DOS 3.3 golden (document /I as the Initech extension). QEMU B032 must finish without keyboard EOF and QUOTES.TXT must print only the matching quoted line. Mutants: always read stdin, stop at the first doubled quote, accept /BAD, or always exit 0; each needs a failing assertion. Scope: One filter parser/result pickup. Do not claim modern FIND error codes are a DOS 3.3 golden; preserve the independently established filter behavior. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite2-B032-BLOCKED.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/B032.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite2-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-find-quotes-exit.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/QUOTES.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-external-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-157.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-158.txt.

title: Apply DOS hidden and system attribute filtering in handle searches
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:3850 limits the special-attribute mask to volume labels and directories, omitting DIR_ATTR_HIDDEN and DIR_ATTR_SYSTEM. command.c:2734 correctly requests directories (0x10), so the backend still returns hidden/system files into ordinary DIR, /W and wildcard listings. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DIR, Reference printed pp.57-58 / PDF142-143; DOS AH=4Eh attribute-mask contract; spec/dos_structs.h. The audit fixture attributes were independently set with mattrib. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend os/milton/test_int21_wildcard.c and test_dir_disk.c with ordinary, H, S, HS, directory and combined attributes, exact and wildcard searches and multiple requested masks. Compare with a real DOS 3.3 DTA golden and mtools fixture inventory. Replay B001/B003 on QEMU; no H/S names may enter ordinary output. Mutant: omit H/S from the search filter; the enumeration and rendered-name assertions must fail. Scope: Fix the shared AH=4Eh/4Fh mechanism, while retaining intentional hidden-file searches by callers that request the attributes; a DIR-only string filter hides the backend bug. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite2-B003-dir-wide.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite2-B001-dir-paths.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite2-B001.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite2-B003.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/preparation.json.

title: Preserve the last completed command template after Ctrl-C
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:1536 gives conin_cooked_line the same buf+2 for output and the saved template. conedit.h:102 overwrites those bytes while typing. The Ctrl-C path at int21.c:1544 skips publishing a new count but does not restore the old bytes; command.c:3632 retains the static AH=0Ah block, so F3 reuses cancelled text with the previous count. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-users-guide/ch8-keys.tex:25-33 says completed Enter commits the template and Ctrl-C discards the unfinished line. MS-DOS 3.3 keyboard-template pages are supporting reference; no new historical claim is needed to enforce this shipped promise. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend harness/conkeys/test_conkeys.c plus the INT21 AH=0Ah wrapper tests: a completed template, a cancelled replacement that is shorter/equal/longer, then F1/F3; include empty input, Escape, Insert and F5 controls. QEMU resume_driver.py keyboard must recall the preceding completed command, never ECHO CANCELED. Mutant: retain the aliasing/no-rollback path; the recalled-byte assertion must fail. Scope: The pure conedit snapshot alone is insufficient: the loss happens in the persistent caller buffer across two AH=0Ah calls. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-keyboard-cancel-template.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-keyboard-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume_driver.py.

title: Render the foreign-MZ refusal reason on the panic screen before halting
description: Root cause: os/milton/loader.c:1138 loader_panic_foreign_mz writes its name and reason only to COM1 at :1141-1148, then executes cli/hlt at :1152. It never calls the framebuffer panic painter. panic_screen.h:37 only supports numeric exception vectors, so a typed loader-reason path is needed rather than inventing a CPU vector. Ground truth: CLAUDE.md Rule 2 and the explicit deliberate-canon foreign-MZ rule; ADR-0003 DEC-08a.5 requires refusal/panic for untagged 16-bit MZ. The requirement is a visible contextual panic, not execution or return to a shell. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add a host rendering assertion for a typed foreign-MZ reason, plus a QEMU foreign-MZ leg using T_DOS16.EXE that captures the screen after the serial HALTED marker. Require PC LOAD LETTER and a readable unsupported 16-bit MZ reason; test-panic must still show ERROR 06 for #UD. Mutant: bypass the framebuffer reason call while retaining serial PANIC/HALTED; the screen assertion must fail. Scope: Do not turn the authorized terminal refusal into recovery or add 16-bit execution. This batch is only the missing visible context. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/prog-mz16-result.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prog-mz16-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/T_DOS16.EXE; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/prepare_special.py.

title: Use one correct environment-expansion path for prompt and batch input
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4887 sends raw interactive input directly to the pipeline dispatcher; batch_expand is called only in run_batch at :4627. os/milton/batch.c:265 deliberately emits an undefined closed variable literally, and test_batch.c:119 currently pins that behavior without an independent period golden. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex, Replaceable Parameters, promises %NAME% as the value; ADR-0003 DEC-11 grounds COMMAND compatibility. The exact interactive, unset, unmatched-percent and percent-escape rules need a real DOS 3.3 golden before replacing existing expectations; the report labels these expectations as memory. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Mint a real DOS 3.3 corpus for defined/unset/mixed-case variables, %% escapes, unmatched percent, %0..%9 and interactive FOR %F versus batch %%F. Extend test_batch and a command-entry C host oracle; expand exactly once before pipe/redirection parsing while preserving FOR syntax. Replay advanced-keyboard and BENV.BAT on QEMU. Mutants: bypass interactive expansion or preserve an unset closed variable in batch; compare against the independent corpus, not the same implementation. Scope: Do not blindly reuse batch %% collapsing at the interactive prompt or expand IF/FOR bodies a second time. Reconcile the existing literal-unset host expectation only after independent reference capture. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/advanced-keyboard-interactive-expansion.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/advanced-keyboard-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-keyboard-recall-kinds.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-keyboard-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-batch-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/BENV.BAT.

title: Provide a secondary interactive COMMAND session with EXIT back to its caller
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4705 rejects every COMMAND invocation that does not begin /C. There is no interactive secondary-prompt entry even though /C already saves private environment and shell-exit context at :4711-4727. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-b.tex:102-104 promises typing commands in a second processor; MS-DOS 3.3 COMMAND, Reference printed pp.46-47. ADR-0003 DEC-11 defines the native interpreter. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the command-session host oracle and a QEMU followup trace: COMMAND -> private SET/PROMPT -> COMMAND /C ECHO NESTED -> EXIT -> parent prompt. Verify the parent environment, CWD/handle rules from the real DOS 3.3 golden, nested depth refusal, and permanent-shell EXIT. Mutant: retain the mandatory /C guard or let EXIT unwind the permanent processor; each must fail the session marker assertions. Scope: Factor an interactive loop that does not rerun SYSINIT/AUTOEXEC or reset the parent state. Coordinate the shared builtin_command epilogue with B05; each remains a separate acceptance item. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-commands-env.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log.

title: Keep batch arguments beyond percent-9 and correct the SHIFT manual
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4650 allocates only ten argv slots and :4670 stops parsing after nine supplied parameters; batch_frame.view[10] at :4444 and the count clamp at :4611 provide no later-argument reservoir for SHIFT. SHIFT at :4575 correctly starts at zero, so %0 changes. pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:247 incorrectly promises %0 is unchanged. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide SHIFT, Reference printed p.151 / PDF236 (evidence/manual-page-236.txt), explicitly describes more than ten parameters and losing the original %0. The shipped nine-argument limit describes the current narrower feature; only the %0 statement is a present documentation defect. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend an execution-level C batch oracle with 11+ short parameters within the command-tail limit, repeated SHIFT through exhaustion, empty arguments and independent nested CALL frames. QEMU B060/TEN must expose ten then eleven in %9 while shifting %0 as DOS does. Correct the Reference comment/text and recorded SHIFT example; run test-pubs-examples and the DOS manual gate. Mutants: stop storing after nine or start shifting at slot one; both must fail independent expected output. Scope: Keep the visible substitution window %0..%9; the missing feature is retaining later command-tail arguments, not adding modern %10 syntax. Correct the separate manual limit when the reservoir ships. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite4-B060-batch-args.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/advanced-misc-errorlevel-shift.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite4-B060.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/ARGS.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/more-fixtures/TEN.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-236.txt.

title: Honor SORT starting columns and reject unsupported options
description: Root cause: os/milton/sort_program.asm:64 scans for /R only and silently advances past every other switch at :76. compare_lines at :272 always starts both pointers at the first byte; no /+n offset exists. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide SORT, Reference printed p.116 / PDF201 (evidence/manual-page-201.txt), defines /R and /+n. Unsupported-option refusal should use an independently captured DOS 3.3 diagnostic/status rather than a new invented success. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test-sort-filter with SORTCOL.TXT, /+1, /+4, reverse plus column, short/empty lines, invalid columns, /BAD and status checks, graded against literal independent results and a real DOS 3.3 argument golden. QEMU followup must put 02 apple before 01 zebra with /+4, and external must refuse /BAD. Mutants: ignore the column offset or accept unknown switches; require both to go red. Scope: Keep the existing explicit capacity refusal and ordinary case-insensitive/reverse comparisons intact; over-capacity truncation was not found by this audit. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/followup-sort-column-cap.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/followup-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/special-fixtures/SORTCOL.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-external-filters.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-external-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-201.txt.

title: Offer the DOS batch-termination question and support continuing with N
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:5337 sets the shell recovery latch; os/milton/command.c:4618 immediately exits the batch loop whenever it is set. There is no batch-specific Y/N decision or resume path for a PAUSE or ECHO/GOTO loop. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide PAUSE, Reference printed p.149 / PDF234 (evidence/resume-manual-page-234.txt). pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:38-39 currently documents immediate cancellation, so this is a missing compatibility feature, not a broken narrow promise. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add a C execution-state oracle and QEMU resume_driver.py batch legs: Ctrl-C at PAUSE and in LOOP.BAT, Y ends and N continues exactly once; test invalid answer, nested CALL and redirected input/output cleanup. Capture real DOS 3.3 behavior for which nested frame is cancelled. Mutant: always terminate or always resume regardless of answer; each must fail a post-question sentinel. Update the manual and its examples with the new behavior. Scope: Depends on reliable resident-call interruption handling from B01; do not use a nonlocal jump that skips open-handle restoration. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-batch-pause-break.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/resume-batch-loop-break.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-batch-serial.log; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/BREAK.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-fixtures/LOOP.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/resume-manual-page-234.txt.

title: Implement DEL directory as confirmed deletion of its contained files
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3321 recognizes delete-all confirmation only for a literal *.* leaf. A non-wildcard directory reaches dos_unlink at :3347, so the backend correctly rejects deleting the directory as a file. No directory-operand expansion to contained files exists at the shell entry. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DEL, Reference printed p.56 / PDF141 (evidence/manual-page-141.txt), explicitly accepts a directory name to delete its files. Backend rejection of unlinking directories must remain. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend the host DOS safety/FAT oracle with a named directory, nested subdirectory, read-only child and 300 ordinary files; N must preserve every byte and Y must delete only eligible immediate files while retaining directories and protected children. Replay B023 under QEMU and verify the stopped image with mtools/fsck.fat. Mutants: route the directory straight to unlink, delete without confirmation, or recurse into children; the state assertions must fail. Scope: Resolve the operand as a directory before transforming it to directory\*.*; retain drive identity and the existing protected-file/no-cap enumeration behavior. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite2-B023-del-directory.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite2-B023.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/extracted/suite2/T/DELDIR/ONE.TXT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-141.txt.

title: Add DATE and TIME entry prompts and TIME fractional-field parsing
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:3469 and :3499 only report the clock when no argument is supplied. The entry loops exist solely in startup_datetime at :3654/:3664. cmd_parse_time at :972 rejects remaining .hundredths text, and dos_settime at :2206 always passes DL=0. int21.c:4924 explicitly ignores fractional seconds because the current RTC seam has one-second resolution. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide DATE printed p.55 / PDF140 and TIME pp.120-121 / PDF205-206 (evidence/manual-page-140.txt, manual-page-205.txt, manual-page-206.txt); spec/int21h_register.json AH=2Ch/2Dh. The shipped manual currently promises display-only/no-fraction forms. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend test_command date/time parsing plus a fake-clock C execution oracle: no-arg entry, blank retains, invalid reprompts, leap-day and range limits, .00/.99 and malformed suffixes. Replay B038/B039 under QEMU; TIME 13:14:15.99 must be accepted and both no-arg commands must request input. Mutation: omit the no-arg prompt or reject the fractional field; require each leg to fail. Document the RTC rounding/resolution contract explicitly rather than claiming retained hundredths without implementing and testing it. Scope: Reuse entry/validation logic without rerunning startup as a side effect; synchronize the Reference syntax and examples when the broader forms ship. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite3-B038-date-formats.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite3-B039-time-values.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite3-B038.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite3-B039.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-140.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-205.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/manual-page-206.txt.

title: Implement prompt-level ECHO state and the blank-line shorthand
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:184 tokenizes ECHO. as a distinct external word and the classify table at :86 recognizes only ECHO. dispatch_control at :4541 updates echo_on only when a batch frame exists; otherwise builtin_echo at :2968 always reports on and :2971 prints OFF/ON as text. No processor-level echo state or ECHO. syntax exists. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide ECHO, Reference printed p.143 / PDF228 (evidence/manual-page-228.txt), defines ON/OFF; ADR-0003 DEC-11. Mint actual DOS 3.3 interactive ON/OFF and ECHO. behavior because the report explicitly labels the blank-line shorthand as memory. Shipped Reference currently documents the narrower prompt behavior. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend command parser/execution host tests with ECHO., ECHO text, ON/OFF/query, @ suppression and CALL/secondary processor state. Replay B036 and advanced-keyboard on QEMU: blank line without Bad command; OFF followed by a query reports off. Grade ECHO. bytes and state lifetime against the real DOS 3.3 golden. Mutants: classify ECHO. externally or keep frame-only state; each must fail. Update both ECHO manual entries and examples. Scope: Define state inheritance/restoration with B11 before changing nested-session semantics; the feature must not consume literal message text as an option unexpectedly. title: Expand PROMPT $V using the native DOS version contract
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:995 cmd_render_prompt has no V/v switch arm; its default at :1147 emits the character literally, producing V>. dos_getver at :2343 already exposes AH=30h, but prompt_ctx_t has no version supplied to the renderer. QEMU promptversion must show the correct version rather than V>; compare formatting to real DOS 3.3 and keep VER/AH=30h consistent. title: Validate BREAK operands against an independently captured DOS grammar
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:2989 recognizes ON/OFF but :2995 silently falls through for every other operand and :3000 reports the unchanged state. This is explicit existing policy, also documented in pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch2-entries-a.tex:67-68; strict invalid-operand reporting was never built. Ground truth: Shipped Reference BREAK syntax at ch2-entries-a.tex:59 and the explicit lenient text at :67-68; ADR-0003 DEC-16 3.3 governs the flag, not invalid command-line wording. The audit supplies only a tester expectation for rejection, so capture a real DOS 3.3 BREAK INVALID/trailing-operand golden before changing the narrow policy. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Add C command-argument tests for empty, mixed-case ON/OFF, INVALID and extra words; assert rejected input never changes the flag. Replay gaps2 on QEMU and grade the chosen diagnostic/status against the DOS 3.3 capture. Mutant: treat an invalid operand as the bare query; the diagnostic assertion must fail if the reference requires rejection. If the reference confirms the present leniency, close this candidate as reference-correct instead of changing code. Update manual text only if the policy changes. Scope: Low-priority compatibility investigation and bounded implementation, not a proven violation of the shipped manual or an authorization to replace its explicit policy from memory. title: Show and clear the MORE indicator at interactive page waits
description: Root cause: os/milton/more_program.asm:125 reaches the page boundary then calls AH=08h directly at :126-127. No marker string is emitted or cleared anywhere in the pagination path. Its existing passthrough path intentionally has no prompt. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide printed p.20 / PDF105 (evidence/resume-manual-page-105.txt) explicitly describes the --More-- indicator. Preserve the existing redirected byte-exact passthrough test and require no indicator bytes there. Mutant: omit the marker write or emit it to redirected stdout; screen and byte checks must catch both. Scope: Only pager feedback; the report proves the waits themselves already work.
